description: Internal curated knowledge-base of 120+ verified, fact-checked human observations and counter-intuitive facts.

items.text: The only part of your reflection you can actually lick is your tongue.
Your brain actively deletes your nose from your vision even though you see it twenty-four seven.
You physically cannot hum while holding your nose shut.
You have never actually seen your own face with your own eyes, only reflections, screens, and photographs.
Your brain uses twenty percent of your body's total energy despite accounting for only two percent of your weight.
Sleeping is just charging your biological battery, while dreaming is running a background diagnostic test.
Every seven years, virtually every single cell in your body has been replaced, making you a completely new person.
Clapping is just repeatedly slapping yourself because you enjoyed something.
Your nervous system has an eighty millisecond transmission delay, meaning you technically live slightly in the past.
The brain named itself, recognized itself, and is right now realizing that exact fact.
Your stomach produces a brand new layer of mucus every two weeks to prevent digesting itself.
You can never touch anything truly at the atomic level, because electron repulsions make you hover over everything.
Your bones are completely wet right now, but you will never feel it.
When you blush, the lining of your stomach also blushes red.
Human eye lenses focus upside down, and your brain permanently flips the image so you do not get confused.
Hearing your voice on a recording sounds wrong because you usually hear it vibrating through your own skull bones.
Fingerprints exist to give your skin friction and allow acoustic vibrations to travel deeper into tactile nerves.
Blinking is a physical screen wipe that your brain intentionally edits out of your conscious memory.
Your tongue is the only muscle in your entire body that is anchored at only one end.
You are a brain piloting a bone mech armor wrapped in meat and powered by bio-electricity.
If unraveled, the DNA in every single cell of your body would stretch to Pluto and back.
Your age is just the number of laps you have survived around a giant nuclear fireball in space.
Yawning cools down your brain when blood temperature inside the cranial cavity rises.
You can easily bite through your own finger with the force you use for a carrot, but your brain refuses to allow it.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
Your shadow is proof that light traveled ninety-three million miles uninterrupted through space just to be blocked by your foot.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus because it rotates slower than it orbits the Sun.
When you look at stars in the night sky, you are looking at ghost light from millions of years ago.
If you fold a single sheet of paper in half forty-two times, its thickness would reach all the way to the Moon.
Oxford University existed for hundreds of years before the Aztec Empire was even founded.
Time moves slightly faster on top of a mountain than at sea level due to gravitational time dilation.
Today is the oldest you have ever been, and the youngest you will ever be for the rest of your life.
There are more trees on planet Earth than there are stars in the entire Milky Way galaxy.
Every clock you look at is just a synchronized estimate created by humanity so we can agree on meetings.
The Sun takes about two hundred and thirty million years to orbit the galaxy, meaning dinosaurs lived on the opposite side of space.
If the history of Earth were compressed into twenty-four hours, humans showed up at eleven fifty-eight at night.
Because the universe expands in all directions, every point in existence can mathematically claim to be the center.
We use calendars to track the past, but we spend our entire existence strictly anticipating the next hour.
Woolly mammoths were still roaming Wrangel Island while workers were building the Egyptian pyramids.
The present moment has no physical thickness; the second you experience it, it instantly transforms into historical data.
Light from the Sun takes eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach Earth, meaning if it disappeared right now, we would not notice.
Space is not completely silent because electromagnetic vibrations can be converted into terrifying audible frequencies.
Neutron stars are so dense that a single teaspoon of their material would weigh six billion tons on Earth.
You are traveling through space right now at over one point three million miles per hour without feeling a breeze.
A teaspoon of water contains more water molecules than there are teaspoons of water in the Atlantic Ocean.
Every photo taken of you captures a younger version of yourself that no longer exists anywhere.
If two pieces of identical metals touch in open space vacuum, they permanently fuse together in cold welding.
The Earth is basically a giant spaceship with life support, but nobody is at the control steering wheel.
Honey never spoils; archaeologists discovered three-thousand-year-old honey inside Egyptian tombs that remains completely edible.
A pizza is a circle, delivered in a square cardboard box, and eaten in triangles.
Bananas share sixty percent of the exact same genetic DNA sequence with human beings.
Nothing is ever on fire. Fire is always on things.
Under specific laboratory pressures, water can boil and freeze at the exact same temperature called the triple point.
If poison expires past its date, does it become more poisonous, or less poisonous?
Apples float in water because twenty-five percent of their physical volume is literally trapped air.
Every book you have ever read is just twenty-six letters arranged in different permutations.
Diamonds are made of pure compressed carbon, meaning a pencil lead and an engagement ring are the same element.
You can never hold an empty container because it is always completely full of room temperature air.
Microwaves heat water molecules directly through dielectric resonance rather than applying outside heat.
Washing dishes is just wiping yesterday's fuel containers so you can refill them with tomorrow's energy.
Peanuts are not actually botanical nuts; they grow underground as legumes related to beans and peas.
Keys are tiny brass sculptures that convince mechanical locks to grant you access to shelter.
Bubble wrap was originally invented in nineteen fifty-seven as textured 3D wallpaper.
Your smartphone has millions of times more computing power than NASA used to land astronauts on the Moon.
Glass is an amorphous solid that behaves like a frozen liquid with disorderly molecular structures.
Ice melts into water, which was the very thing you used to make the ice in the first place.
The smell of freshly cut grass is actually a distress chemical signal released by the plant under attack.
A refrigerator is a box that spends electricity to keep heat outside so your food rots slower.
Vanilla flavoring originally used vanillin derived from wood pulp lignin fibers.
Mirrors in stores are angled slightly backwards to create slimming optical perspective illusions.
Matchsticks were invented three years after the invention of mechanical pocket lighters.
Soap does not kill most bacteria; it just makes your skin so slippery they slide down the drain.
Trees communicate underground and share nutrients through vast fungal mycelium networks called the wood wide web.
Sharks existed before Saturn developed its rings and before trees even evolved on Earth.
Octopuses have three hearts, blue hemocyanin blood, and two-thirds of their neurons reside inside their tentacles.
A caterpillar turns into complete genetic liquid soup inside its cocoon before reforming into a butterfly.
Sloths can hold their breath underwater for forty minutes, significantly longer than dolphins.
Every drop of water you drink has circulated through dinosaurs and ocean clouds millions of times.
Crows recognize individual human faces and pass grudges down to their offspring across generations.
Pigeons used to deliver critical wartime messages, and now they just bob their heads outside train stations.
Lightning strikes planet Earth approximately eight million times every single day.
Animals in the wild probably think we are strange hairless creatures that build giant square caves.
The immortal jellyfish can revert its mature cells back into polyp infancy when injured or starving.
Clouds look light and fluffy, but an average cumulus cloud weighs over one million pounds of water.
Butterflies taste surfaces through sensory receptors located on their feet.
Plants are technically farming humans by producing oxygen until we die and decompose into fertilizer.
A blue whale's tongue weighs as much as an entire adult Asian elephant.
The ocean floor has deep-sea trenches unexplored, while we send rovers across the sands of Mars.
Honeybees communicate complex flower coordinates by performing rhythmic waggle dance angles relative to the sun.
Bats are the only mammals capable of true sustained aerodynamic flight.
Ants do not have lungs; oxygen enters through microscopic valve holes along the sides of their bodies.
If you look closely at sand under a microscope, each tiny grain is a miniature tumbled gemstone.
Flamingos are born grey and turn bright pink entirely from consuming carotenoid pigments in brine shrimp.
Rain does not have a smell of its own; petrichor is the scent of soil bacteria aerosolized by raindrops.
Sea otters hold paws while sleeping so currents do not drift them away from each other.
Earth has survived five mass extinctions, but we act like climate change will destroy the planet instead of us.
If you replace every single part of an axe over time, does it remain the exact same axe?
You can never prove that anyone else experiences consciousness the same way you do.
Your brain constantly invents false memories every time you recall an event, editing the story slightly.
The word abbreviation is remarkably long for a word that literally means making something shorter.
The McGurk effect proves that what your eyes see can literally alter the sound your ears hear.
If you are waiting for the waiter, you are technically the waiter in that moment.
Deja vu occurs when sensory input bypasses short-term processing and deposits directly into long-term memory.
You cannot imagine a brand new color that does not already exist within the visible spectrum.
Your future self is watching you right now through the memories you are creating today.
The Tetris effect causes people who play repetitive games to see patterns moving in the dark when closing their eyes.
Every secret you keep is proof that two different versions of you exist simultaneously.
Phantom vibration syndrome makes over eighty percent of phone owners feel vibrations when their phone never buzzed.
You can read this sentence without speaking a word, yet a distinct voice is talking inside your head.
Saying 'do not think of a pink elephant' immediately forces your neural cortex to render a pink elephant.
Saccadic masking blinds you for forty minutes every single day while your eyeballs dart around between focus points.
The alarm clock is the only device designed specifically for you to hate the sound of it.
Placebos can still trigger genuine neurological relief even when doctors tell patients it is a fake sugar pill.
Every decision you have ever made has led you directly to reading this exact word right now.
We laugh at dogs chasing their tails, but humans spend decades chasing imaginary validation.
Capgras delusion causes people to believe their closest family members have been replaced by identical impostors.
You spend the first half of your life wanting to be older, and the second half wishing you were younger.
If practice makes perfect, but nobody is perfect, why do we practice?
Cognitive dissonance physically activates the anterior cingulate cortex, the same region that registers acute physical pain.
Which is why you should never overthink these...
